summary: Full regression of AuthContext refactor + QR/Biometric feature-flag work. 17/17 backend pytest cases passed (auth, platform settings defaults & persistence, QR scan happy path + all forbidden branches + regenerate history preservation, global QR OFF blocks, per-school QR OFF blocks, biometric locked unless BOTH global and per-school flags ON). Frontend: Founder login, session-persist-after-reload, and logout all work; Platform Settings renders the new 'Attendance Features' section with QR toggle (default ENABLED) and Biometric toggle (default DISABLED); toggling either and saving persists across reload, and reverts cleanly. Camera-based QR *capture* is not exercised (no device) — the /api/qr/scan endpoint is exhaustively tested by direct POSTs using real student qr_tokens, which is the equivalent guarantee. No regressions introduced by the AuthContext / QrAttendancePanel edits.
critical_code_review_comments: QrAttendancePanel.jsx uses student `name` as the React map key for the 'Marked Present' list. Two different students with the same display name (very possible in schools) will collide and hide one entry. Prefer a stable id like student_id (returned by /qr/scan) as the key.

routes_qr.py `student_view` returns id/name/roll/class/section/photo but does NOT include the school-scoped student_id explicitly — the frontend can consume `student.id`, but the response would be more resilient if it also returned `attendance_id` for optimistic UI updates.

auth_utils.py qr_enabled_for_school() treats a missing school document as False (correct), but returns True for a school whose `qr_attendance` field is missing (default-on). This is intentional per spec; just note that any older schools created before this field existed silently participate in QR — desired behaviour, documented for clarity.

AuthContext.refreshMe: current catch always sets user=false on any error, which is correct, but for transient network errors this forces a login redirect. Consider distinguishing network errors from 401 in the future (low priority).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (login, reload-persistence, logout, settings defaults, QR toggle persistence, Biometric toggle persistence)

test_credentials: Founder mahatofauji@gmail.com / ManiFounder@2026 (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). All other accounts were created and hard-deleted by the test.
seed_data_creation: Two temp schools (code prefix TSTQR*) with admins, one class+section+teacher+student each plus an 'other-class' student, were created via the API for the QR scan matrix. All hard-deleted at teardown along with derived users, classes, sections and attendance rows. Platform settings restored to qr_attendance=true, biometric_attendance=false. Final DB state matches pre-test baseline (1 pre-existing 'Mani Public School' school + 1 admin + 1 founder).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable regression suite is /app/backend/tests/test_qr_attendance.py — run with `pytest tests/test_qr_attendance.py -v -o addopts=''` from /app/backend. The suite is self-contained: creates its own schools/users, hard-deletes them at teardown and restores platform QR flag. Camera QR *capture* on the UI cannot be run headlessly; the equivalent /api/qr/scan security matrix is fully covered here.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. The AuthContext.jsx catch-block refactor (log-and-set-user-false in login/logout/refreshMe) and QrAttendancePanel.jsx catch-block warn + React map key change did not regress any behaviour. Auth, session, and QR scan API all behave correctly.
